page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-64 is a dedicated x86_64 compute instance engineered with 64 dedicated virtual CPUs and 512 GB of system memory. Operating within a high-memory tier, the architecture allocates an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without integrated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs, and relies entirely on external network-attached storage configurations given the lack of integrated local storage.

Hardware resource distribution favors substantial primary memory footprint requirements alongside multi-threaded processing. The provision of 64 dedicated compute threads paired with 512 GB of memory prevents memory contention in large single-node environments. Because local ephemeral or NVMe disks are not provided, system I/O throughput is coupled directly to attached persistent storage services, requiring consideration of virtual disk attachment limits and storage fabric bandwidth.

From an operational efficiency standpoint, the high memory density per compute core optimizes cost allocation for systems bottlenecked by RAM rather than raw compute cycles. Workloads benefiting most from this provisioning profile include extensive in-memory caching layers, medium-to-large database engines, distributed processing coordinator nodes, large data transformations, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-64 is an x86_64 architecture cloud instance equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of memory, delivering an expanded memory profile of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Designed for applications prioritizing memory capacity over attached disk or accelerator resources, the instance does not feature local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached persistent storage for filesystem operations. This structural design makes it effective for memory-bound computational tasks that require substantial RAM allocations across a balanced thread count without paying resource overhead for unused local NVMe storage or specialized hardware accelerators. Core deployment scenarios encompass high-capacity in-memory databases, large-scale caching platforms, intensive batch data manipulation, enterprise resource planning services, and distributed compute workloads requiring extensive memory per execution thread.
